Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): discretionary spend and complex regulatory cases in a regime that sells complexity. memo.verdict: Park. Neutral; conviction medium (a Triaging record from research alone, with the post-results sell-side response missing from the evidence and the sell-side earnings-momentum pin absent). Bally's Intralot is a 'Major Corporate Change' case that is not compelling at EUR 1.077 (2026-09-22): the change is real at every input, but the UK gaming duty and the debt taken on to build the group have so far cancelled it in the outputs, and the return needs a re-rating that only deleveraging can earn while the company keeps spending the deleveraging on the next deal. The park rule applies on its own terms: management is a D (three of the framework's red flags fit: dangerous leverage, a debt-funded buyback, empire-building) and the record does not argue otherwise; business quality C, predictability C and trackability C, so the park rests on management alone. Not bearish, because the price is not demanding, the operating delivery is real and a cleared branch is a C; not bullish, because the modal return is a D and the things that would make it a B are the things management keeps deferring. The case would clear the bar on the modal path below about EUR 0.80 (three years) to EUR 0.91 (eighteen months); it cleared it at EUR 0.90 in March 2026. Events that reopen it: a reported leverage print at or below 3.8x with Evoke consolidated, or a year without a deal.
case: - The change inside the company is broad and real, and it is the case. In October 2025 a Greek lottery-technology supplier bought BII, tripled its revenue, took the acquirer's chief executive and its 58 percent parent, and became a UK-centred online casino operator with a long-contract lottery business as ballast. Seven of twelve internal forces are strong, above the screen's threshold of three; the actions are resourced and dated (EUR 41 million synergy programme; dividend; buyback; Evoke). Three red flags sit beside the forces (leverage 4.05x heading to 4.5x; a buyback at that leverage; a second acquisition eight months after the first); they do not remove the change, they set its cost.

- The external force is a first-order headwind that arrived at the same time: Remote Gaming Duty to 40 percent (EUR 34.0 million in Q2 2026, 65 percent offset in the quarter, the rest resting on H2 2026 cuts), and General Betting Duty to 25 percent enacted for April 2027. The same duty is the consolidation opening the strategy is built on: sub-scale operators exit, and the group would be number two in UK online by gross gaming revenue with Evoke.

- The change reached the operating metrics and stopped there. UK online +11.6 percent constant currency in Q2 2026 through the duty doubling; net gaming revenue at a record. It has not reached the financial statements as improvement (pro-forma EBITDA EUR 399.9 million and 37.2 percent margin below EUR 430.8 million and 39.7 percent; leverage 4.05x from 3.50x; reported loss) nor the estimates as upgrades (FactSet mean earnings per share FY2026 to FY2028 cut 8 to 10 percent over six months while targets rose and the buy share went to 100 percent: brokers like the story and have been lowering the numbers, the profile of a stock waiting for proof). The 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain holds through four layers and breaks at the fifth and sixth; the break is the duty and the leverage, not the operations.
counter_case: - At its strongest: the debt-funded consolidation is a rational, value-creating response to a once-in-a-generation dislocation, not an overreach. The 40 percent duty removes the UK online tail and hands share to the scaled: Tier Two and below took 7 percent of share since 2021 and are expected to give it back. Evoke at 52 pence, with GBP 180 million of synergies against GBP 25 million of cost and 99.63 percent shareholder approval, is an irreplaceable database bought at a distressed price; Lottomatica has just shown a levered online consolidator can deliver synergies 50 percent above plan (EUR 119 million run-rate) and trade at the 90th percentile of its history. Vitruvian and PlayerX give real marketing efficiency: spend 10 points below peers, growth without dilutive promotion. The lottery book is a sixteen-year contracted floor; free cash flow of EUR 89.0 million in a half after EUR 117.4 million of capital expenditure shows the cash engine works; the chief executive took Gamesys from 3.8x to 1.1x in two years. At 11.5x adjusted earnings and about 7x EV/EBITDA the price already discounts the leverage, so a return to 3x by FY2028 re-rates the shares to 13 to 14x and, with 13 percent earnings growth and a 2 percent yield, gives 20 percent a year. Jefferies' EUR 1.35 target and the 100 percent buy share are this hypothesis in the market.

- Conceded: the operating evidence is genuinely strong (mitigation delivered, not promised; UK growth accelerated through the duty; the 2026 contract wins are real); the price is not demanding against peers; the cleared branch is a C on our own arithmetic (14.4 percent a year at 13.5x) and higher on consensus earnings; the reported loss is largely amortisation of acquired intangibles and deal costs, which the market is right to look through in part.
triggers: - Invalidate levels: UK constant-currency online revenue growth below 5 percent for two consecutive quarters after the H2 2026 cuts; adjusted net leverage above 3.8x at end FY2027; less than GBP 120 million of Evoke synergies by the end of year two; more than two further major contract losses by mid-2027.

- Alarm levels: UK growth below 8 percent in any quarter; leverage not below 4.0x at end FY2026; Illinois RFP not awarded to the group, or a second renewal at a fee cut of Montana's size; a Fitch downgrade or an Evoke financing that raises starting leverage above about 4.5x; active players falling in any quarter; BII 2026 synergy run-rate short of EUR 15 million; annualised net finance cost not falling by the FY2027 results; a further rise in parent payables or a parent capital call; a further earnings-per-share cut of 2 percent or more after the Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-27.

- What would reopen the case: a reported leverage print at or below 3.8x at end FY2026 with Evoke consolidated; an equity-funded Evoke structure that lowers the starting point; a year without a deal or a stated leverage covenant on new acquisitions; the price below about EUR 0.80 to 0.91.

- What would move the setup fit to B: Q3 and Q4 2026 results showing the H2 mitigation closing the remaining 35 percent and adjusted earnings-per-share estimates rising, moving maturity to full output.
- What would move management to C and lift the park rule: Evoke financing closing on a structure that lowers leverage from the start, and four quarters without a further deal.
- What would change our side on each driver: UK growth below 5 percent in Q3 and Q4 2026 with active players falling; an Illinois RFP to a rival; a year without a deal.
